reason: This book's mandate is a long-only, equal-weight basket of wide-moat, high-ROIC compounders held through volatility, not traded tactically around it -- and nothing in this week's research broke that thesis for any of the ten names. NAV is +4.33% since the 7/17 entry, ahead of SPY (+2.73%), with a modest -3.27% max drawdown and 90/10 gross/cash -- the book is doing exactly what it was built to do. I checked the four legs with the largest recent moves or news flow (WebSearch budget was exhausted this session, so I used WebFetch on stockanalysis.com instead, as flagged): ORCL (+16.77% leg P&L) shows a genuine yellow flag -- roughly $18B of loans tied to an Oracle-leased AI data center are reportedly trading at 89-91 cents on the dollar, a real credit-market stress signal on the AI-capex buildout, and the stock has been volatile -- but FY26 revenue is still +17% YoY, cloud backlog remains large, and 43 analysts still rate it Buy with material upside to target; this is a risk to monitor, not yet a moat impairment, so I am not cutting a 9% position over it this week. AVGO (-3.56%) and LLY (-2.08%) both look fundamentally intact and even strengthening -- Broadcom's AI infrastructure demand commentary from management was reaffirmed despite sector-wide AI-spending jitters, and Lilly is taking meaningful US oral-GLP1 share from Novo alongside a new FDA breast-cancer approval, both still carrying strong Buy consensus. COST (-4.69%) has slowing membership growth (+4% YoY) and mixed pre-earnings analyst notes ahead of its 9/24 print (after this book's 9/21 entry), which is worth watching next week but is not itself a reason to sell into an earnings date blind. None of MSFT, AAPL, GOOGL, V, MA or ADP showed any thesis-breaking news in the packet's marks or in what I could still check. Given all ten legs remain investable quality names with intact or improving fundamentals, replacing the book would only add turnover cost (2bps/side plus SEC fees across ten equal-weighted legs) for no identified edge; holding the existing equal-weight, 10%-cash structure is the higher-expected-value choice this week.
